title: Ops Chronicle: replayable incident indexer and lightweight admin CLI
creator: Aisha Verma
description:
Problem: Oncall and SRE teams spend significant time reconstructing incidents (logs, traces, KV snapshots, request payloads) when triaging production outages. Existing runbooks are developer-centric and fragile for partial-rollback/replay scenarios. We need a lightweight indexer that extracts a minimal, scrubbed incident snapshot (chronicle) and exposes a reproducible, permissioned replay surface via a CLI and sandboxed runner.

Proposal: Build 'Ops Chronicle' — a service and admin CLI that: 
- Ingests incident artifacts (trace IDs, request IDs, relevant logs, small KV cache snapshots) and produces a chronicle ID referencing a compact, scrubbed snapshot stored in S3 (or private blob store).
- Produces a deterministic, taskified sequence (runbook-as-data) called a chronicle manifest: ordered micro-steps with inputs and safe-mode guards.
- Exposes a lightweight CLI (ops-chronicle) for engineers to fetch, inspect a minimap (high-level action timeline), and replay the chronicle in a dedicated sandbox or dry-run mode.
- Integrates with RBAC and audit logging so replays are gated and recorded; auto-scrubs PII by default and supports pluggable scrubbers per customer privacy rules.

Design notes: 
- Chronicle manifest format: line-oriented JSONL with step metadata (type, duration estimate, required-perms, trace refs). Keep schema simple to allow ergonomic transformation into existing task runners.
- Storage: objects are immutable and signed; manifest includes a snapshot-signature to detect tampering.
- Replay harness: uses the existing runlet-executor API but with a safe facade (read-only connectors, no external writes unless explicit 'approve' flag and elevated role).
- Observability: each chronicle references Grafana dashboard panels and Datadog trace IDs. The CLI can produce a shareable evidence bundle for postmortems.

Why this is different: Instead of ad-hoc 'playbooks' captured in tickets or PRs, chronicle creates a canonical, replayable artifact that reduces time-to-triage and enables deterministic regression testing against incident reproducers. It complements, not replaces, existing runbooks or the Chronos scheduler.

Risks & mitigations: 
- PII leakage: default scrubber + mandatory manual review for any export beyond internal sandboxes.
- Unsafe writes during replay: default dry-run, write-capability only via token exchange and RBAC approval flows.
- Storage bloat: enforce retention policies and size quotas, compress snapshots and prefer delta snapshots where possible.

Implementation steps (high level): 
1) Manifest schema + serializer/deserializer library (Go + TypeScript).
2) Indexer service (small worker) that assembles manifest from logs/traces/KV (first pass: only request ID and KV keys referenced by traces).
3) ops-chronicle CLI to fetch, inspect, and trigger sandboxed replay (initial UX: list / show / replay --dry-run).
4) Sandbox runner integration and RBAC/audit wiring.
5) E2E tests using synthetic incidents; add a dashboard panel for chronicle usage and time-to-replay metric.

Success metrics: 
- Median time-to-first-repro from incident-open to sandboxed-replay < 20 minutes for top-30 incidents.
- >30% reduction in oncall escalations for identical issues across multiple environments.
- 95% of chronicle-created replays complete in dry-run without manual patches.

comments: 2026-03-02 — Spike complete: prototype indexer extracts trace->KV crosswalk for two sample incidents. Results in PR (12345). Noted that trace sampling must be coordinated with tracing team; added dependency.
2026-03-04 — Design review with SRE/Oncall: agreed default scrubber ruleset; product asked for minimap prototype (timeline of 10s of steps). Action: Jordan to produce CLI minimap UX by 3/9.
2026-03-06 — Security review kickoff: request for threat model around replayed credentials; decided to use ephemeral tokens tied to audit entries. Assigned to Marco Rossi for token flow design.

2026-03-08 — PR feedback on prototype: use immutable signed objects for manifests; hide raw payloads behind ACLs. See inline review comments: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12345/files

2026-03-10 — Integration test (staging): replay dry-run of sample chronicle completed in 12 minutes end-to-end. Observed two flaky steps due to service timeouts — added retry/backoff to manifest runner. Next: add RBAC checks and audit events.
2026-03-10 — Notes from UX session: minimap should show 'confidence' per step (high/medium/low) based on source artifact fidelity. Added label 'confidence' to manifest schema draft.
acceptance_criteria: Indexer produces a chronicle manifest for an incident given a trace ID and associated request IDs
CLI can fetch a chronicle manifest and show a human-readable minimap of steps
Dry-run replay executes in sandbox and emits telemetry and an audit event
PII scrubber runs by default and prevents exporting raw payloads without explicit allowed role
Retention policy enforced and manifests are signed/immutable
